ceilingSources.residentMemoryBytes: rule: 2x the larger measured resident set (62046208 B over the recorded hosts), rounded up to a whole MiB; evidence runtime-budget.evidence/
ceilingSources.idleCpuPercent: rule: 1 percent absolute for an idle crate; measured at most 0.053 percent on the recorded hosts
ceilingSources.wakeupsPerSecond: design bound: neither watchdog thread polls; idle it is one heartbeat wake-up per heartbeat period (1 s) plus one watchdog wake-up per threshold, about 1.2 per second with the defaults (src/watchdog.rs module doc, Wake-ups), doubled and rounded up for the host event loop: 3 per second. The 9.4 and 13.4 per second in macos-arm64-0.3.0.txt are the earlier 250 ms poll the module doc says was removed
ceilingSources.diskOpsPerSecond: design bound: the watchdog threads touch only atomics, the wake bell and the callback (src/watchdog.rs module doc), so the crate issues no disk operations; 1 per second absolute, the sibling crates' floor. Windows measures it (GetProcessIoCounters); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter

status.note: The status call returns rightkit_child_process::ProcessUsage (resident and footprint bytes, cumulative CPU seconds, wake-up and disk-operation totals where the host reports them) beside the crate's own queue figures; the rates come from two calls (ProcessUsage::rates_since). Wake-ups are macOS only; disk operations are Windows and Linux only.

notes: Ceilings come from the recorded measurements by stated rules (ceilingSources); a ceiling left null names its reason below. wakeupsPerSecond and diskOpsPerSecond are design bounds (see ceilingSources); the 0.3.0 evidence (9.4 per second) predates the non-polling watchdog, so a fresh measurement is required; no Windows disk measurement exists and macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter.
